subject: math
cluster: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions

items.prompt:
Two figures are congruent if one maps onto the other by a sequence of:
A) Dilations
B) Rigid motions
C) Any transformations
D) Rotations only

steps: Congruence is defined by rigid motions.

items.prompt:
Congruent figures have corresponding sides that are:
A) Proportional
B) Equal in length
C) Always vertical
D) Unrelated

steps: Rigid motions preserve distance, so sides are equal.

items.prompt:
Which transformation would make two figures NOT congruent?
A) Translation
B) Rotation
C) Reflection
D) Dilation

steps: A dilation changes size, breaking congruence.

items.prompt:
Figure $B$ is a reflection then translation of figure $A$. Figures $A$ and $B$ are:
A) Similar but not congruent
B) Congruent
C) Not related
D) Larger and smaller

steps: Both steps are rigid motions, so they are congruent.

items.prompt:
A square of side $5$ and a square of side $10$ are:
A) Congruent
B) Similar but not congruent
C) Neither
D) The same square

steps: Different sizes means similar, not congruent.

items.prompt:
Congruent figures always have equal:
A) Colors
B) Areas
C) Positions
D) Names

Which statement is true?
A) All similar figures are congruent
B) All congruent figures are similar
C) Congruent figures can have different side lengths
D) Dilations preserve congruence
items.answer: B) All congruent figures are similar

steps: Congruent figures are the special similar case with scale factor $1$.

items.prompt:
Two triangles cannot be mapped onto each other by any sequence of rigid motions. They are:
A) Congruent
B) Not congruent
C) Similar
D) Identical

steps: No rigid-motion sequence means not congruent.
